label: Law of Sines & Law of Cosines
overview: When a triangle is not a right triangle, you cannot use basic SOH-CAH-TOA. The Law of Sines relates sides to the sines of their opposite angles; the Law of Cosines generalizes the Pythagorean theorem to any triangle. SAT questions give you enough information (sides and/or angles) to identify which law applies and solve for the unknown.

workedExamples.problem: In triangle ABC, angle A = 35°, angle B = 70°, and side a = 10. Find side b.

steps.title: Choose Law of Sines (two angles, one side)
steps.content: We know two angles and the side opposite one of them — perfect for Law of Sines.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Law of Sines when you have two sides and the included angle (SAS)
commonMistakes.fix: SAS requires Law of Cosines. Law of Sines needs an angle opposite a known side.

commonMistakes.mistake: Pairing the wrong side with the wrong angle
commonMistakes.fix: Side a is always opposite angle A (lowercase = uppercase rule). Label the triangle before writing any formula.

quickTip: Two angles + any side → Law of Sines. Two sides + included angle OR all three sides → Law of Cosines.
